pob.text: David said to him[a], “What happened? Please tell me.” He said, “The people fled from the battle, and many of the people also fell and died[c][b]; and Saul and Jonathan his son are also dead.”

spob.text:
David asked him, “What happened? Please tell me.”

He answered, “The troops fled from the battle. Many of them fell and died. Saul and his son Jonathan are dead too.”

pob.text: So I stood over him and put him to death[a], because I knew that he would not live after he had fallen. Then I took the crown that was on his head and the armlet that was on his arm[b], and I brought them here to my lord.

public_domain_references.brenton: And it came to pass when a man came near to do him obeisance, that he stretched out his hand, and took hold of him, and kissed him.

pob.text: Absalom did this to all Israel who came to the king for judgment[a], and Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel.

public_domain_references.kjv: And on this manner did Absalom to all Israel that came to the king for judgment: so Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel.
public_domain_references.brenton: And Abessalom did after this manner to all Israel that came to the king for judgment; and Abessalom gained the hearts of the men of Israel.

pob.text: And at the end of forty years, Absalom said to the king, “Please let me go and pay the vow that I vowed to the LORD in Hebron.”

spob.text: After forty years had passed, Absalom said to the king, “Please let me go and pay the vow I made to the LORD in Hebron.”

pob.text: For your servant made a vow while I was dwelling in Geshur in Aram[a], saying, ‘If Yahweh indeed brings me back to Jerusalem[c][b], then I will serve Yahweh.’

pob.text: The king said to him, “Go in peace.” So he arose and went to Hebron.

pob.text: Then Absalom sent spies throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, “As soon as you hear the sound of the trumpet, then say, ‘Absalom has become king in Hebron.’”

pob.text: Two hundred men from Jerusalem went with Absalom[a], invited, and they went innocently, not knowing anything.

pob.text: And Absalom sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite[a], David’s counselor, from his city, from Giloh, while he was offering the sacrifices. And the conspiracy grew strong[c][b], and the people kept increasing with Absalom.

pob.text: Then a messenger came to David[a], saying, “The hearts of the men of Israel are with Absalom.”

pob.text: Then David said to all his servants who were with him in Jerusalem[a], “Arise, and let us flee, for there will be no escape for us from Absalom. Hurry to depart[c][b], lest he quickly overtake us and bring disaster upon us and strike the city with the edge of the sword.”

spob.text: Then David told all his servants who were with him in Jerusalem, “Get up! Let’s flee, or none of us will escape from Absalom. Leave at once, or he may quickly catch us, bring disaster on us, and kill the people in the city with the sword.”

public_domain_references.kjv: And David said unto all his servants that [were] with him at Jerusalem, Arise, and let us flee; for we shall not [else] escape from Absalom: make speed to depart, lest he overtake us suddenly, and bring evil upon us, and smite the city with the edge of the sword.

pob.text: The king’s servants said to the king[a], “Whatever my lord the king chooses, here are your servants.”

spob.text: The king’s servants said to him, “My lord the king, we are your servants, ready to do whatever you choose.”

pob.text: Then the king said to Ittai the Gittite[a], “Why are you also going with us? Return and stay with the king[c][b], for you are a foreigner and also an exile from your own place.”

pob.text: You came only yesterday[a], and today should I make you wander with us, while I go wherever I can go? Return, and take your brothers back with you[c][b]. May steadfast love and faithfulness be with you.

I indeed will go whithersoever I may go: return then, and cause thy brethren to return with thee, and may the Lord deal mercifully and truly with thee.

pob.text: Then Ittai answered the king and said[a], “As Yahweh lives, and as my lord the king lives, surely in whatever place my lord the king may be, whether for death or for life[b], there your servant will be.”

pob.text: The king said to them[a], “What seems good in your eyes, I will do.” So the king stood beside the gate[c][b], and all the people went out by hundreds and by thousands.

public_domain_references.bsb: Your servant could go with the king only a short distance past the Jordan; why should the king repay me with such a reward?
public_domain_references.web: Your servant will just go over the Jordan with the king. Why should the king repay me with such a reward?
public_domain_references.asv: Thy servant would but just go over the Jordan with the king: and why should the king recompense it me with such a reward?
public_domain_references.kjv: Thy servant will go a little way over Jordan with the king: and why should the king recompense it me with such a reward?
public_domain_references.brenton: I am this day eighty years old: can I then distinguish between good and evil? Can thy servant taste any longer what I eat or drink? can I any longer hear the voice of singing men or singing women? and wherefore shall thy servant any longer be a burden to my lord the king?

pob.text: For your servant would only cross the Jordan a little way with the king[a]; why should the king repay me with this reward?

spob.text: For I, your servant, would go with you only a short distance across the Jordan. Why should you repay me with this reward?

public_domain_references.bsb: Please let your servant return, that I may die in my own city near the tomb of my father and mother. But here is your servant Chimham. Let him cross over with my lord the king, and do for him what is good in your sight.”
public_domain_references.web: Please let your servant turn back again, that I may die in my own city, by the grave of my father and my mother. But behold, your servant Chimham; let him go over with my lord the king; and do to him what shall seem good to you.”
public_domain_references.asv: Let thy servant, I pray thee, turn back again, that I may die in mine own city, by the grave of my father and my mother. But behold, thy servant Chimham; let him go over with my lord the king; and do to him what shall seem good unto thee.
public_domain_references.kjv: Let thy servant, I pray thee, turn back again, that I may die in mine own city, [and be buried] by the grave of my father and of my mother. But behold thy servant Chimham; let him go over with my lord the king; and do to him what shall seem good unto thee.
public_domain_references.brenton: Thy servant will go a little way over Jordan with the king: and why does the king return me this recompense?

pob.text: Please let your servant return[a], that I may die in my own city, by the grave of my father and my mother. But here is your servant Kimham; let him cross over with my lord the king[b], and do for him what is good in your eyes.

spob.text: Please allow me, your servant, to return home. I want to die in my own city, near where my father and mother are buried. But here is your servant Kimham. Let him cross the Jordan with you, my lord the king, and do for him whatever seems good to you.

public_domain_references.bsb: The king replied, “Chimham will cross over with me, and I will do for him what seems good in your sight, and I will do for you whatever you desire of me.”
public_domain_references.web: The king answered, “Chimham shall go over with me, and I will do to him that which shall seem good to you. Whatever you request of me, that I will do for you.”
public_domain_references.asv: And the king answered, Chimham shall go over with me, and I will do to him that which shall seem good unto thee: and whatsoever thou shalt require of me, that will I do for thee.
public_domain_references.kjv: And the king answered, Chimham shall go over with me, and I will do to him that which shall seem good unto thee: and whatsoever thou shalt require of me, [that] will I do for thee.
public_domain_references.brenton: Let, I pray thee, thy servant remain, and I will die in my city, by the tomb of my father and of my mother. And, behold, thy servant Chamaam shall go over with my lord the king; and do thou to him as it seems good in thine eyes.

pob.text: Then the king said[a], “Let Kimham cross over with me, and I will do for him what seems good in your eyes; and whatever you choose to lay on me, I will do for you.”

spob.text: Then the king said, “Kimham will cross the Jordan with me. I will do for him whatever you think is best, and I will do whatever you ask of me.”

public_domain_references.bsb: So all the people crossed the Jordan, and then the king crossed over. The king kissed Barzillai and blessed him, and Barzillai returned home.
public_domain_references.web: All the people went over the Jordan, and the king went over. Then the king kissed Barzillai and blessed him; and he returned to his own place.
public_domain_references.asv: And all the people went over the Jordan, and the king went over: and the king kissed Barzillai, and blessed him; and he returned unto his own place.
public_domain_references.kjv: And all the people went over Jordan. And when the king was come over, the king kissed Barzillai, and blessed him; and he returned unto his own place.
public_domain_references.brenton: And the king said, Let Chamaam go over with me, and I will do to him what is good in my sight; and whatsoever thou shalt choose at my hand, I will do for thee.

pob.text: All the people crossed the Jordan[a], and the king crossed over. Then the king kissed Barzillai and blessed him, and he returned to his own place.

spob.text: All the people crossed the Jordan River, and the king also crossed. Then the king kissed Barzillai and blessed him. Barzillai returned to his own place.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Then the king went on to Gilgal, and Chimham crossed over with him. All the troops of Judah and half the troops of Israel escorted the king.
public_domain_references.web: So the king went over to Gilgal, and Chimham went over with him. All the people of Judah brought the king over, and also half the people of Israel.
public_domain_references.asv: So the king went over to Gilgal, and Chimham went over with him: and all the people of Judah brought the king over, and also half the people of Israel.
public_domain_references.kjv: Then the king went on to Gilgal, and Chimham went on with him: and all the people of Judah conducted the king, and also half the people of Israel.
public_domain_references.brenton: And all the people went over Jordan, and the king went over; and the king kissed Berzelli, and blessed him; and he returned to his place.

pob.text: Then the king crossed over to Gilgal[a], and Kimham crossed over with him. And all the people of Judah escorted the king across, and also half the people of Israel.

spob.text: Then the king crossed the Jordan on his way to Gilgal, and Kimham crossed with him. All the people of Judah helped the king cross[a], along with half the people of Israel.

public_domain_references.bsb: Soon all the men of Israel came to the king and asked, “Why did our brothers, the men of Judah, take you away secretly and bring the king and his household across the Jordan, together with all of David’s men?”
public_domain_references.web: Behold, all the men of Israel came to the king, and said to the king, “Why have our brothers the men of Judah stolen you away, and brought the king and his household, over the Jordan, and all David’s men with him?”
public_domain_references.asv: And, behold, all the men of Israel came to the king, and said unto the king, Why have our brethren the men of Judah stolen thee away, and brought the king, and his household, over the Jordan, and all David’s men with him?
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ And, behold, all the men of Israel came to the king, and said unto the king, Why have our brethren the men of Judah stolen thee away, and have brought the king, and his household, and all David’s men with him, over Jordan?
public_domain_references.brenton: And the king went over to Galgala, and Chamaam went over with him: and all the men of Juda went over with the king, and also half the people of Israel.

pob.text: And behold[a], all the men of Israel came to the king and said to the king, “Why have our brothers, the men of Judah, stolen you away and brought the king and his household across the Jordan[b], and all David’s men with him?”

spob.text: Now all the men of Israel came to the king and asked him, “Why did our brothers, the men of Judah, steal you away[a] and bring you, your household, and all David’s men across the Jordan?”

public_domain_references.bsb: And all the men of Judah replied to the men of Israel, “We did this because the king is our relative. Why does this anger you? Have we ever eaten at the king’s expense or received anything for ourselves?”
public_domain_references.web: All the men of Judah answered the men of Israel, “Because the king is a close relative to us. Why then are you angry about this matter? Have we eaten at all at the king’s cost? Or has he given us any gift?”
public_domain_references.asv: And all the men of Judah answered the men of Israel, Because the king is near of kin to us: wherefore then are ye angry for this matter? have we eaten at all at the king’s cost? or hath he given us any gift?
public_domain_references.kjv: And all the men of Judah answered the men of Israel, Because the king [is] near of kin to us: wherefore then be ye angry for this matter? have we eaten at all of the king’s [cost]? or hath he given us any gift?
public_domain_references.brenton: And behold, all the men of Israel came to the king, and said to the king, Why have our brethren the men of Juda stolen thee away, and caused the king and all his house to pass over Jordan, and all the men of David with him?

pob.text: Then every man of Judah answered the man of Israel[a], “Because the king is a close relative to me[b]. So why has this matter made you angry? Have we eaten at all at the king’s expense? Or has he given us any gift?”

spob.text: Then the men of Judah answered the men of Israel, “The king is our close relative. Why are you angry about this? Have we eaten anything at the king’s expense? Or has he given us any gift?”[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: “We have ten shares in the king,” answered the men of Israel, “so we have more claim to David than you. Why then do you despise us? Were we not the first to speak of restoring our king?” But the men of Judah pressed even harder than the men of Israel.
public_domain_references.web: The men of Israel answered the men of Judah, and said, “We have ten parts in the king, and we have also more claim to David than you. Why then did you despise us, that our advice should not be first had in bringing back our king?” The words of the men of Judah were fiercer than the words of the men of Israel.
public_domain_references.asv: And the men of Israel answered the men of Judah, and said, We have ten parts in the king, and we have also more [right] in David than ye: why then did ye despise us, that our advice should not be first had in bringing back our king? And the words of the men of Judah were fiercer than the words of the men of Israel.
public_domain_references.kjv: And the men of Israel answered the men of Judah, and said, We have ten parts in the king, and we have also more [right] in David than ye: why then did ye despise us, that our advice should not be first had in bringing back our king? And the words of the men of Judah were fiercer than the words of the men of Israel.
public_domain_references.brenton: And all the men of Juda answered the men of Israel, and said, Because the king is near of kin to us: and why were you thus angry concerning this matter? have we indeed eaten of the king's food? or has he given us a gift, or has he sent us a portion?

pob.text: There happened to be there a worthless man[a], whose name was Sheba son of Bichri, a Benjaminite. He blew the trumpet and said, “We have no share in David, and no inheritance in the son of Jesse. Every man to his tents[d][c][b], O Israel!”

spob.text: There was a worthless man[a] there named Sheba son of Bichri, from the tribe of Benjamin. He sounded the trumpet[b] and said, “We have no share in David’s rule and no inheritance in the son of Jesse. People of Israel, every man should return to his own home or camp!”[c]

public_domain_references.bsb: Now a worthless man named Sheba son of Bichri, a Benjamite, happened to be there, and he blew the ram’s horn and shouted: “We have no share in David, no inheritance in Jesse’s son. Every man to his tent, O Israel!”
public_domain_references.web: There happened to be there a wicked fellow, whose name was Sheba the son of Bichri, a Benjamite; and he blew the trumpet, and said, “We have no portion in David, neither have we inheritance in the son of Jesse. Every man to his tents, Israel!”
public_domain_references.asv: And there happened to be there a base fellow, whose name was Sheba, the son of Bichri, a Benjamite: and he blew the trumpet, and said, We have no portion in David, neither have we inheritance in the son of Jesse: every man to his tents, O Israel.
public_domain_references.kjv: And there happened to be there a man of Belial, whose name [was] Sheba, the son of Bichri, a Benjamite: and he blew a trumpet, and said, We have no part in David, neither have we inheritance in the son of Jesse: every man to his tents, O Israel.
public_domain_references.brenton: And there was a transgressor [so] called there, and his name was Sabee, a Benjamite, the son of Bochori: and he blew the trumpet, and said, We have no portion in David, neither have we [any] inheritance in the son of Jessæ: to thy tents, O Israel, every one.

pob.text: So every man of Israel went up from following David to follow Sheba son of Bichri[a], but the men of Judah held fast to their king[b], from the Jordan to Jerusalem.

spob.text: So all the men of Israel went away from David and followed Sheba son of Bichri. But the men of Judah held fast to their king from the Jordan to Jerusalem.

public_domain_references.bsb: So all the men of Israel deserted David to follow Sheba son of Bichri. But the men of Judah stayed by their king all the way from the Jordan to Jerusalem.
public_domain_references.web: So all the men of Israel went up from following David, and followed Sheba the son of Bichri; but the men of Judah joined with their king, from the Jordan even to Jerusalem.
public_domain_references.asv: So all the men of Israel went up from following David, and followed Sheba the son of Bichri; but the men of Judah clave unto their king, from the Jordan even to Jerusalem.
public_domain_references.kjv: So every man of Israel went up from after David, [and] followed Sheba the son of Bichri: but the men of Judah clave unto their king, from Jordan even to Jerusalem.
public_domain_references.brenton: And all the men of Israel went up from following David after Sabee the son of Bochori: but the men of Juda adhered to their king, from Jordan even to Jerusalem.

pob.text: When David came to his house at Jerusalem[a], the king took the ten women, the concubines whom he had left to keep the house, and put them in guarded custody and provided for them, but he did not go in to them. So they were kept confined until the day of their death[c][b], living as widows.

spob.text: When David returned to his home in Jerusalem, he took the ten concubines[a] he had left to guard the house and placed them under guard. He provided for them, but he did not have sexual relations with them. They remained confined until they died, living like widows even though David was still alive.

public_domain_references.bsb: When David returned to his palace in Jerusalem, he took the ten concubines he had left to care for the palace, and he placed them in a house under guard. He provided for them, but he no longer slept with them. They were confined until the day of their death, living as widows.
public_domain_references.web: David came to his house at Jerusalem; and the king took the ten women his concubines, whom he had left to keep the house, and put them in custody and provided them with sustenance, but didn’t go in to them. So they were shut up to the day of their death, living in widowhood.
public_domain_references.asv: And David came to his house at Jerusalem; and the king took the ten women his concubines, whom he had left to keep the house, and put them in ward, and provided them with sustenance, but went not in unto them. public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ And David came to his house at Jerusalem; and the king took the ten women [his] concubines, whom he had left to keep the house, and put them in ward, and fed them, but went not in unto them. So they were shut up unto the day of their death, living in widowhood.
public_domain_references.brenton: And David went into his house at Jerusalem: and the king took the ten women his concubines, whom he had left to keep the house, and he put them in a place of custody, and maintained them, and went not in to them; and they were kept living as widows, till the day of their death.

pob.text: Then the king said to Amasa[a], “Call the men of Judah together for me within three days, and you, remain here.”

spob.text: Then the king said to Amasa, “Gather the men of Judah[a] for me within three days. You yourself must stay here.”

public_domain_references.bsb: Then the king said to Amasa, “Summon the men of Judah to come to me within three days, and be here yourself.”
public_domain_references.web: Then the king said to Amasa, “Call me the men of Judah together within three days, and be here present.”
public_domain_references.asv: Then said the king to Amasa, Call me the men of Judah together within three days, and be thou here present.
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ Then said the king to Amasa, Assemble me the men of Judah within three days, and be thou here present.
public_domain_references.brenton: And the king said to Amessai, Call to me the men of Juda for three days, and do thou be present here.

pob.text: So Amasa went to summon Judah[a], but he delayed beyond the appointed time that he had set for him.

spob.text: So Amasa went to call the people of Judah together,[a] but he was late—past the time David had set for him.

public_domain_references.bsb: So Amasa went to summon Judah, but he took longer than the time allotted him.
public_domain_references.web: So Amasa went to call the men of Judah together, but he stayed longer than the set time which had been appointed to him.
public_domain_references.asv: So Amasa went to call [the men of] Judah together; but he tarried longer than the set time which he had appointed him.
public_domain_references.kjv: So Amasa went to assemble [the men of] Judah: but he tarried longer than the set time which he had appointed him.
public_domain_references.brenton: And Amessai went to call Juda, and delayed beyond the time which David appointed him.

pob.text: Then David said to Abishai[a], “Now Sheba son of Bichri will do us more harm than Absalom. You, take your lord’s servants and pursue after him, lest he find fortified cities for himself and escape from our sight.”

spob.text: Then David said to Abishai, “Sheba son of Bichri will now do us more harm than Absalom did. You must take my servants and go after him. Otherwise, he may find fortified cities for himself and escape from our sight.”

public_domain_references.bsb: And David said to Abishai, “Now Sheba the son of Bichri will do us more harm than Absalom. Take your lord’s servants and pursue him, or he will find fortified cities and elude us.”
public_domain_references.web: David said to Abishai, “Now Sheba the son of Bichri will do us more harm than Absalom did. Take your lord’s servants and pursue after him, lest he get himself fortified cities, and escape out of our sight.”
public_domain_references.asv: And David said to Abishai, Now will Sheba the son of Bichri do us more harm than did Absalom: take thou thy lord’s servants, and pursue after him, lest he get him fortified cities, and escape out of our sight.
public_domain_references.kjv: And David said to Abishai, Now shall Sheba the son of Bichri do us more harm than [did] Absalom: take thou thy lord’s servants, and pursue after him, lest he get him fenced cities, and escape us.
public_domain_references.brenton: And David said to Amessai, Now shall Sabee the son of Bochori do us more harm than Abessalom: now then take thou with thee the servants of thy lord, and follow after him, lest he find for himself strong cities, so will he blind our eyes.

pob.text: Joab’s men[a], the Kerethites, the Pelethites, and all the mighty men went out after him. They went out from Jerusalem to pursue Sheba son of Bichri.

spob.text: Joab’s men, the Kerethites[a], the Pelethites, and all the mighty warriors followed him. They left Jerusalem to pursue Sheba son of Bichri.

public_domain_references.bsb: So Joab’s men, along with the Cherethites, the Pelethites, and all the mighty men, marched out of Jerusalem in pursuit of Sheba son of Bichri.
public_domain_references.web: Joab’s men went out after him with the Cherethites, the Pelethites, and all the mighty men; and they went out of Jerusalem to pursue Sheba the son of Bichri.
public_domain_references.asv: And there went out after him Joab’s men, and the Cherethites and the Pelethites, and all the mighty men; and they went out of Jerusalem, to pursue after Sheba the son of Bichri.
public_domain_references.kjv: And there went out after him Joab’s men, and the Cherethites, and the Pelethites, and all the mighty men: and they went out of Jerusalem, to pursue after Sheba the son of Bichri.
public_domain_references.brenton: And there went out after him Amessai and the men of Joab, and the Cherethites, and the Phelethites, and all the mighty men: and they went out from Jerusalem to pursue after Sabee the son of Bochori.

pob.text: When they were by the great stone that is in Gibeon[a], Amasa came before them. Now Joab was dressed in his military garment, and over it was a belt with a sword fastened to his waist in its sheath; and as he went out[c][b], it fell.

spob.text: When they were beside the great stone at Gibeon, Amasa approached them.[a] Joab was wearing his military garment. Over it, he wore a belt that held a sheathed sword at his waist. As Joab went out, the sword fell.

public_domain_references.bsb: And while they were at the great stone in Gibeon, Amasa joined them. Now Joab was dressed in military attire, with a dagger strapped to his belt. And as he stepped forward, he slipped the dagger from its sheath.
public_domain_references.web: When they were at the great stone which is in Gibeon, Amasa came to meet them. Joab was clothed in his apparel of war that he had put on, and on it was a sash with a sword fastened on his waist in its sheath; and as he went along it fell out.
public_domain_references.asv: When they were at the great stone which is in Gibeon, Amasa came to meet them. And Joab was girded with his apparel of war that he had put on, and thereon was a girdle with a sword fastened upon his loins in the sheath thereof; and as he went forth it fell out.
public_domain_references.kjv: When they [were] at the great stone which [is] in Gibeon, Amasa went before them. And Joab’s garment that he had put on was girded unto him, and upon it a girdle [with] a sword fastened upon his loins in the sheath thereof; and as he went forth it fell out.
public_domain_references.brenton: And they [were] by the great stone that is in Gabaon: and Amessai went in before them: and Joab had upon him a military cloak over his apparel, and over it he was girded with a dagger fastened upon his loins in its scabbard: and the dagger came out, it even came out and fell.

pob.text: Joab said to Amasa[a], “Is it well with you, my brother?” And Joab took hold of Amasa’s beard with his right hand to kiss him.

spob.text: Joab said to Amasa,[a] “Is all well with you, my brother?” Then Joab took Amasa by the beard with his right hand to kiss him.

public_domain_references.bsb: “Are you well, my brother?” Joab asked Amasa. And with his right hand Joab grabbed Amasa by the beard to kiss him.
public_domain_references.web: Joab said to Amasa, “Is it well with you, my brother?” Joab took Amasa by the beard with his right hand to kiss him.
public_domain_references.asv: And Joab said to Amasa, Is it well with thee, my brother? And Joab took Amasa by the beard with his right hand to kiss him.
public_domain_references.kjv: And Joab said to Amasa, [Art] thou in health, my brother? And Joab took Amasa by the beard with the right hand to kiss him.
public_domain_references.brenton: And Joab said to Amessai, Art thou in health, [my] brother? and the right hand of Joab took hold of the beard of Amessai to kiss him.

pob.text: But Amasa was not on guard against the sword that was in Joab’s hand[a], and he struck him with it in the belly, and his entrails spilled out to the ground; he did not strike him again, and he died. Then Joab and Abishai his brother pursued Sheba son of Bichri.

spob.text: But Amasa was not watching out for the sword in Joab’s hand. Joab struck him in the belly[a] with it, and his entrails spilled onto the ground. Joab did not strike him a second time; Amasa died. Then Joab and his brother Abishai pursued Sheba son of Bichri.

public_domain_references.bsb: Amasa was not on guard against the dagger in Joab’s hand, and Joab stabbed him in the stomach and spilled out his intestines on the ground. And Joab did not need to strike him again, for Amasa was dead. Then Joab and his brother Abishai pursued Sheba son of Bichri.
public_domain_references.web: But Amasa took no heed to the sword that was in Joab’s hand. So he struck him with it in the body and shed out his bowels to the ground, and didn’t strike him again; and he died. Joab and Abishai his brother pursued Sheba the son of Bichri.
public_domain_references.asv: But Amasa took no heed to the sword that was in Joab’s hand: so he smote him therewith in the body, and shed out his bowels to the ground, and struck him not again; and he died. And Joab and Abishai his brother pursued after Sheba the son of Bichri.
public_domain_references.kjv: But Amasa took no heed to the sword that [was] in Joab’s hand: so he smote him therewith in the fifth [rib], and shed out his bowels to the ground, and struck him not again; and he died. So Joab and Abishai his brother pursued after Sheba the son of Bichri.
public_domain_references.brenton: And Amessai observed not the dagger that was in the hand of Joab: and Joab smote him with it on the loins, and his bowels were shed out upon the ground, and he did not repeat the blow, and he died: and Joab and Abessai his brother pursued after Sabee the son of Bochori.

pob.text: And one of Joab’s young men stood over him and said[a], “Whoever favors Joab, and whoever is for David[b], follow Joab!”

spob.text: One of Joab’s men[a] stood over him and said, “Whoever supports Joab, and whoever is loyal to David, follow Joab!”

public_domain_references.bsb: One of Joab’s young men stood near Amasa and said, “Whoever favors Joab, and whoever is for David, let him follow Joab!”
public_domain_references.web: One of Joab’s young men stood by him, and said, “He who favors Joab, and he who is for David, let him follow Joab!”
public_domain_references.asv: And there stood by him one of Joab’s young men, and said, He that favoreth Joab, and he that is for David, let him follow Joab.
public_domain_references.kjv: And one of Joab’s men stood by him, and said, He that favoureth Joab, and he that [is] for David, [let him go] after Joab.
public_domain_references.brenton: And there stood over him one of the servants of Joab, and said, Who [is] he that is for Joab, and who [is] on the side of David following Joab?

pob.text: Amasa was wallowing in blood in the middle of the highway. When the man saw that all the people were stopping[a], he moved Amasa from the highway into the field and threw a garment over him, because he saw that everyone who came upon him stopped.

spob.text: Amasa was in the middle of the highway, writhing[a] in blood. The man saw that all the people were stopping, so he moved Amasa off the highway into a field and covered him with a garment. He did this because everyone who came upon Amasa stopped.

public_domain_references.bsb: But Amasa wallowed in his blood in the middle of the road, and when the man saw that all the troops were stopping there, he dragged the body off the road into a field and threw a garment over it.
public_domain_references.web: Amasa lay wallowing in his blood in the middle of the highway. When the man saw that all the people stood still, he carried Amasa out of the highway into the field, and cast a garment over him when he saw that everyone who came by him stood still.

Or will you flee three months before your adversaries while they pursue you? Or shall there be three days of pestilence in your land? Now know and see what answer I should return to the one who sent me.”

pob.text: Then David said to Gad[a], “I am in great distress. Let us fall, please, into the hand of Yahweh, for his mercies are many[b]; but let me not fall into the hand of man.”
